Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1228 AM CDT Thu Jul 30 2026

Valid 311200Z - 011200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM IOWA
SOUTHWARD INTO THE OZARK PLATEAU...AND OVER THE CENTRAL AND SOUTHERN
HIGH PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
At least isolated severe storms appear possible from Iowa southward
into the Ozark Plateau, and over the central and southern High
Plains Friday afternoon and evening. Sporadic occurrences of
damaging wind and large hail will be the primary hazards with a
conditional risk for a few tornadoes, mainly in Missouri.

...Synopsis...

A short-wave trough from the upper Midwest into mid MO Valley Friday
morning will translate into the mid MS Valley with a belt of 30-35
kt winds forecast within the western through southern periphery of
that feature. At the surface, an area of low pressure is expected to
undergo slight deepening while developing from northwest or central
IA at the start of the period into southern IL by late Friday night.
Meanwhile, a trailing cold front will advance south/southeast into
the southern Plains and Ozark Plateau.


...Lower Missouri and mid Mississippi Valleys into the Ozark
Plateau...

Mainly elevated showers and thunderstorms are expected to be ongoing
at 12Z Friday across portions of IA and MO within a zone of forcing
for ascent ahead of the mid-level system, and warm advection and
moisture transport along a 30-40 kt low-level jet. Those mechanisms
are likely to sustain deep convection through the morning into
afternoon east of the surface low, mainly across IL. In the wake of
the early-day storms and where cloud breaks can occur, daytime
heating combined with boundary-layer dewpoints in the low to mid 70s
is expected to yield a relatively narrow axis of moderate
instability with MLCAPE of 1000-2500+ J/kg.

Additional surface-based storms are expected to develop by early- to
mid afternoon initially near the surface low in south-central or
southeast IA with subsequent southward development along or ahead of
the front across MO. The 00Z CAMs suggest that the initial storm
mode will be semi-discrete, which is consistent with model forecasts
of 30-35 kt deep-layer shear vectors oriented largely perpendicular
to the initiating boundary. 

While some marginally severe hail is possible with any supercell
structures, warm mid-level temperatures will contribute to
considerable melting, potentially limiting that threat. Damaging
wind potential may be limited by storm mode with a more substantial
threat being dependent on upscale growth into clusters or a
cold-pool-driven MCS. Tornado potential remains unclear as the
models suggest the strongest low-level shear will remain displaced
to the east of the primary instability axis. That being said, a
conditional threat for a few tornadoes appears possible with: 1)
storms forming near or to the south of the surface low, should
modest low-level CAPE develop in the presence of locally enhanced
vertical vorticity, and 2) any supercells that can form in the warm
sector and move east into the stronger low-level shear forecast
across eastern MO during the late afternoon into evening. 

Given the above uncertainties, a level 1/Marginal Risk will be
maintained with this forecast.


...Colorado and New Mexico...

Initially northerly, post-frontal winds Friday morning are expected
to switch to northeast and then east by afternoon into evening,
supporting isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms along favored
terrain. MLCAPE on the order of 1000-2000 J/kg will coincide with
30-35 kt of deep-layer shear, suggesting the potential for at least
transient supercell structures capable of large hail. With time,
storms may grow upscale into clusters with a relatively deep,
well-mixed boundary layer enhancing the potential for locally severe
wind gusts. This is especially the case across parts of eastern NM
Friday evening where the merging of the terrain-induced storms and
cold-frontal storms could organize a more substantial cold pool.

..Mead.. 07/30/2026

$$

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0227 PM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

Valid 311200Z - 011200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM CENTRAL
IOWA ACROSS MUCH OF MISSOURI AND INTO NORTHERN ARKANSAS...AND OVER
PARTS OF THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
At least isolated severe storms appear possible from Iowa southward
into the Ozarks, and over the central and southern High Plains
Friday afternoon and evening.

...IA/MO/AR...
A shortwave trough is forecast to develop out of the northern Plains
and move southeastward toward the mid MS Valley Friday, with
increasing midlevel northwesterlies to over 40 kt. At the surface,
low pressure should develop from southern IA into northern MO during
the day, moving into western IL by 12Z Saturday. 

Upper 60s to lower 70s F dewpoints will be common ahead of an
associated cold front which will extend roughly across southern IA
and into central MO during the peak heating hours. While midlevel
lapse rates will not be particularly steep, MLCAPE over 2000 J/kg is
still forecast. Further, winds will veer with height, resulting in
semi-favorable hodographs for supercells with deep layer shear over
30 kt.

Early day rain appears likely from southern MN into IA and MO as the
initial warm/moist advection occurs, with diurnal storms expected
along the front during the late afternoon. The stronger storms may
produce hail, a brief tornado, or damaging wind gusts. Placement of
such a narrow north/south risk area has inherent uncertainties this
far out, but a corridor of greater severe probabilities could be
required in later outlooks as predictability increases.

...Eastern CO/NM...
Northwest flow aloft on the order of 20-30 kt will exist over the
High Plains on the backside of the shortwave trough to the
northeast. Surface winds will veer to east/northeasterly by late
afternoon as peak heating is attained. Dewpoints into the 50s F,
steep low-level lapse rates and modest northwest flow aloft should
yield a few cells capable of marginally severe hail or wind.

..Jewell.. 07/29/2026

$$

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0339 AM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

Valid 011200Z - 061200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Day 4/Saturday...

A short-wave trough will progress from the mid MS into lower OH
Valleys with modest height falls forecast across the Gulf Coast
states. At the surface, an area of low pressure will follow the same
track as the upper-air system, while a trailing cold front advances
through the lower MS and TN Valleys. While weaker than on Friday, a
modest enhancement of 850-mb winds is forecast during the afternoon
ahead of the surface low over the OH and TN Valleys. 

Morning storms appear possible from the lower OH into lower MS
Valleys within a zone of warm advection associated with a nocturnal
low-level jet. The longevity and extent of early-day storms remain
uncertain, but where stronger heating can occur, the presence of
boundary-layer dewpoints in the 70s will contribute to pockets of
moderate instability. Additional storms are anticipated during the
afternoon, focused along the cold front and any residual outflow
boundaries from previous storms. Deep-layer shear is expected to
remain generally less than 30 kt, which will tend to limit the
potential for organized storm modes. A possible exception is across
parts of KY and TN where slightly stronger low-level shear could
contribute to updraft rotation and some tornado risk. Otherwise,
locally damaging wind gusts appear to be the primary hazard.

Isolated severe storms capable of mainly damaging winds and hail
appear possible over the southern High Plains Saturday afternoon and
evening within a moist and unstable upslope regime. 


...Days 5 and 6/Sunday and Monday...

The models remain in relatively good agreement in depicting a strong
short-wave trough and attending belt of mid-level flow progressing
along the international border from the northern Rockies into the
northern Plains. Low-level ridging from the Great Lakes into
southern Plains may disrupt the return of robust boundary-layer
moisture ahead of a cold front moving through the northern Plains
into the upper MS Valley. Nonetheless, the presence of steep lapse
rates and strengthening vertical shear along the frontal zone will
support some severe weather risk over the northern Plains on Sunday
and the northern Plains into the upper MS Valley on Monday.

An isolated severe storm threat may also develop along the East
Coast on Sunday, ahead of a positively tilted trough moving through
the Great Lakes and OH and TN Valley. 


...Days 7 and 8/Tuesday and Wednesday...

The 00Z ensemble means indicate a belt of modestly enhanced
mid-level flow from the northern Rockies into the Great Lakes,
between a trough over Hudson Bay and a flattened ridge across the
Southwest. Some severe weather threat may materialize over the
central High Plains along and to the north of a stalled front, and
perhaps in AZ if stronger easterly flow can develop on the south
side of the upper high.

..Mead.. 07/29/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0746 PM CDT Wed Jul 29 2026

Valid 300100Z - 301200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM PARTS OF
NORTHERN MINNESOTA SOUTHWESTWARD INTO THE WESTERN DAKOTAS...IN
NORTHERN FLORIDA AND IN PARTS OF THE INTERMOUNTAIN WEST...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with isolated severe wind gusts and hail will be
possible this evening into the early overnight from parts of
northern Minnesota southwestward into the western Dakotas.
Additional severe gusts could occur in northern Florida and in parts
of the Intermountain West.

...Northern Minnesota/Dakotas/Western Nebraska...
A subtle shortwave trough is evident on water vapor imagery over the
northern High Plains. A sufficiently moist airmass is located ahead
of the trough from the central and western Dakotas, where surface
dewpoints are generally in the upper 50s and 60s F. Scattered strong
thunderstorms are ongoing near a gradient of moderate instability
from central North Dakota southwestward into western South Dakota.
Along this gradient, surface-temperature dewpoint spreads are
generally in the 30 to 40 degree F range, and the RAP has 0-3 km
lapse rates in the 8 to 8.5 C/km range. This should support an
isolated potential for severe wind gusts early this evening. Hail
could also occur with the stronger cells. An isolated severe threat
could persist into the late evening and early overnight in parts of
northern North Dakota and northern Minnesota, as the shortwave
trough moves eastward across the region.

...Northern Florida...
The latest water vapor imagery shows a mid-level shortwave trough
along the Eastern Seaboard. At the surface, an outflow boundary is
located across northern Florida, along which scattered thunderstorms
are ongoing. Surface dewpoints to the south of the outflow boundary
are mostly in the 70s F. This is contributing to moderate
instability, with the RAP showing MLCAPE in the 2500 to 3000 J/kg
range. This thermodynamic environment may support a potential for
isolated severe gusts early this evening.

...Intermountain West...
A mid-level shortwave trough is currently evident on water vapor
imagery over southeastern Idaho. Scattered thunderstorms are being
supported by large-scale ascent associated with this trough. In
addition, a small pocket of instability is analyzed by the RAP over
southeast Idaho, where MLCAPE is around 1000 J/kg. The instability
combined with steep low to mid-level lapse rates could support
isolated severe wind gusts early this evening.

..Broyles.. 07/30/2026
